messages:
alex: Heads-up — cross-lang SDK release targeted today at 18:00 PT. Plan: staged rollout (start small -> ramp), publish npm + pypi artifacts, deprecate legacy sync client with docs banner. Need QA signoff and final decision on holdback percentages. Who can take smoke tests?

maya: I can run the integration smoke on staging, give me the must-pass checklist and I’ll run in ~30m.

alex: Must-pass: auth flows, streaming, function-calls, telemetry headers, and ensure existing sync API still works for consumers. Also verify artifacts are signed (GPG) and checksums match.

sam: Staggered rollout sounds good. My suggestion: start 5% for 20–30m, then 25% for 45m, then 100 if stable. Also add a runtime fallback flag so we can flip traffic back instantly. @alex do we want automated rollback on error thresholds?

jen: I’ll draft the deprecation banner and a concise migration guide (sync -> async patterns). Need the planned removal date and whether we want an opt-out period.

chris: Release notes: include breaking changes, migration snips, and caching/kv notes. I’ll open the draft PR now: https://github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/1950 (will add checklist). Also will include artifact checksums.

deploy-bot: Canary publish scheduled for 2026-03-20T18:20:00Z (unix 1950125000). Targets: npm @redwood/sdk@canary and python redwood-sdk==0.9.0rc1. Reply with `approve` to start the pipeline.

maya: approve (I’ll post results as soon as staging tests finish).

alex: approve as well. @sam please watch metrics: alert if 5xx rate > 0.5% or p95 latency increases by >20% vs baseline. Also watch error traces in Sentry.

sam: on it. I’ll spin up a temp dashboard and hook an alert to #incidents.

jen: Proposed deprecation removal date: 2026-09-30. I’ll add a banner to docs and a migration note in the changelog. If that works I’ll include the copy in the release PR.

chris: Uploaded checksums to the PR: `sha256:3b1f9d2c4a6e...` and `sha256:9a7c1f0b8d2c...`. Will request GPG sigs from release engineers before final publish.

alex: One more: TypeScript peerDep decision — do we require a minimum TS major? We should avoid hard pins if possible.

sam: Recommend peerDep min >=4.5.0, not a hard pin. That keeps older projects working but nudges modern toolchains.

deploy-bot: Publish pipeline started (canary): logs available at https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/195012-publish. First step: build artifacts -> wheel, sdist, tarball.

maya: staging smoke: auth ok, streaming ok, small mismatch in chunking behavior during long streams — logging a note in the QA checklist.

alex: good catch. If that affects p95 we'll hold the ramp. @sam please correlate with canary telemetry.

sam: seeing small uptick in p95 for the stream endpoint (about 12%). 5xx rate still low. Holding ramp for now.

jen: I’ll delay the deprecation announcement until we confirm stream behavior is stable. Will still push the migration guide PR.

chris: If we need a quick mitigation, we can publish a patch to the runtime adapter that reverts the new chunking heuristic. I can open a follow-up PR if we decide.

alex: consensus: hold ramp, block full rollout until stream p95 within 7% of baseline. Keep canary active at 5%. Jen — keep deprecation copy ready, but don’t post banner yet.

deploy-bot: Canary pipeline still running. Current status: artifacts built, published to canary registry, traffic at 5%. Next check scheduled in 15m.

maya: QA run complete — logs attached to the PR. No functional regressions besides streaming p95 note.

sam: monitoring only. I’ll add a short-lived alert to automatically notify us if 5xx > 0.3% during canary.

alex: thanks all. If we hit stability target (p95 delta < 7%) we’ll proceed with ramp plan. Otherwise we’ll either patch runtime or revert. I’ll update the release PR with these gating decisions. :thumbsup:

chris: ack, will be ready to PR a runtime patch if needed.

jen: migration guide ready in draft, waiting on stream decision to finalize wording.

deploy-bot: Last automated status update: canary at 5%, next automated metric check at unix 1950125600.
